$schema_note: Design modifications and transition steps for moving the Northwoods pilot from its as-written design to a defensible one. Consumed by tools/transition_pathways.py. Cost and benefit figures trace to cost_basis_2026.json and REFERENCES.md; scheduling, consent and reversibility parameters are ASSUMPTIONS and are marked as such.

_effort_model._note: Effort converts heterogeneous friction into dollars so leverage is a single ratio. All four weights are ASSUMPTIONS — vary them and re-run; the ranking is stable across a wide band, which is the point worth checking.
_effort_model._irreversibility_note: Applied as penalty * (1 - reversibility). A cheap decision that forecloses a later option is not cheap.
_effort_model._knee_rule: smallest prefix capturing 90% of total positive value

modifications.name: Selective burial instead of blanket burial
modifications.change: Bury only where burial buys something: urban and highway crossings, wildfire-ignition corridors, icing-exposed spans, sensitive habitat. Overhead elsewhere.
modifications.rationale: Buried cable costs about 4.5x the equivalent overhead line. The as-written design buries all 4,500 km without ever pricing the alternative, which makes it the largest unexamined cost decision in the programme.
modifications._buried_fraction_note: 20% covers urban crossings and high-consequence corridors in a mostly rural three-state footprint. The right number comes from a routing study (step T1), not from this file.
modifications._reversibility_note: Fully reversible until construction starts on a given segment.

modifications.name: HVAC default; HVDC only where distance justifies converters
modifications.change: Specify HVAC for the network. Reserve HVDC for individual runs over roughly 500-600 km — in this footprint that is the long lake crossings, not the backbone.
modifications.rationale: Converter stations are 30-40% of HVDC project capex and are a fixed cost per terminal, so HVDC loses to HVAC below roughly 500-600 km. A 4,500 km network of shorter segments is the wrong shape for HVDC. The repository never makes this choice, which leaves a 30-40% capex swing unresolved.
modifications._reversibility_note: Reversible on paper; expensive once converter procurement starts.

modifications.name: Reallocate the over-budgeted lines to transmission and storage
modifications.change: Move the derived surplus from the compute, software and workforce lines into transmission and storage, holding the total envelope fixed.
modifications.rationale: The re-derivation found compute over-allocated by roughly 240x, software by 14x and workforce by 6x, while transmission was understated by 1.9x. The envelope was approximately right; the allocation inside it was not. This is a spreadsheet change, not a funding request.

modifications.name: Specify grid-forming inverters at procurement
modifications.change: Require IEEE 2800-2022 with amendment 2800a grid-forming capability on every inverter-based resource intended to island or black-start.
modifications.rationale: Grid-forming inverters establish voltage and frequency autonomously and provide synthetic inertia; grid-following inverters need an existing grid reference and cannot black-start. Every 'graceful collapse buffering' and 'restart locally' claim in this repository is a grid-forming capability. It does not fall out of the routing software, and it is not a retrofit.
modifications._premium_note: Order-of-magnitude. Grid-forming control is largely firmware plus headroom; the premium is small at procurement and very large as a retrofit.
modifications._reversibility_note: Effectively one-way. Not specifying it now forecloses islanding for the asset's life.

modifications.name: Substitute storage for marginal transmission kilometres
modifications.change: Site storage at load pockets to defer the most expensive marginal line segments rather than building transmission to serve peak.
modifications.rationale: Stationary storage packs fell 45% in 2025 to $70/kWh, and installed systems run $150-250/kWh. Transmission runs $5.0-10.1M/km. There is now a real trade between the two that did not exist when the design was written.
modifications._deferred_km_note: Needs a production-cost model to size properly. 400 km of ~4,500 is a deliberately conservative placeholder.

modifications.name: Anchor tenant: contract the load before building for it
modifications.change: Sign a large interconnecting load — data centre, electrolyser, or industrial process — to a long-term contract before committing transmission capital.
modifications.rationale: EIA's 2026 outlook makes data centre load the dominant driver of US electricity growth, and this is how transmission is actually being financed in 2025-26. It converts a speculative ratepayer-funded build into contracted revenue, which is the difference between needing a benefit-cost case and having a counterparty. The region already has the two things such a tenant wants: cold water and cheap wind.
modifications._note: This changes who pays, not what gets built. It is listed as a modification because it changes the design's financial structure, which is the part that currently does not close.
modifications._cost_note: ASSUMPTION — development, legal and interconnection study costs to reach a signed contract.

modifications.name: Phase-gate on measured reliability, not asserted reliability
modifications.change: Replace the '99.95% reliability achieved' expansion trigger with a measured SAIDI/SAIFI improvement gate on the built phase, evaluated against the pre-build baseline.
modifications.rationale: Every 99.95% figure in this repository is a target and none has been validated. An expansion gate that tests an unmeasured quantity is not a gate. Measuring it is also how the reliability benefit term gets populated.

steps.name: Fund the reliability valuation study (LBNL ICE Calculator)
steps.note: The single largest missing term in the benefit-cost case. Until it exists, the project's own analysis understates it.

steps.name: Routing and undergrounding study
steps.note: Determines which segments genuinely need burial. Gates both M1 and M5, and is the cheapest way to resolve the largest cost uncertainty in the programme.

steps.name: Adopt the claim-sourcing rule as programme governance
steps.note: Already in force in this repository (CONTRIBUTING.md). Listed because a programme that reintroduces unsourced figures at the financing stage loses its credibility exactly when it needs it.

steps.name: Tri-state compact (MN-WI-MI)
steps.note: Three legislatures plus three governors. The long pole in the governance path.

steps.name: MISO transmission planning submission and interconnection position
steps.note: MTEP cycle entry. Also the prerequisite for any anchor tenant, since a tenant is buying a queue position as much as a site.

steps.name: State certificates of need (one per state)
steps.note: Requires a benefit case. Filing before the reliability study exists means filing the weak version of your own argument.

steps.name: Tribal nation consultation and partnership agreements
steps.note: Sovereign nations, not stakeholders. Routing crosses treaty-ceded territory; consultation gates siting and is far cheaper to start early than to retrofit around.

steps.name: Federal corridor designation (NIETC or equivalent)
steps.note: Optional. Unlocks federal backstop siting and some financing programmes; costs political capital in exchange for reduced state veto risk.

steps.name: Choose cost recovery: rate base vs merchant vs hybrid
steps.note: Rate base spreads cost across captive ratepayers and needs a PUC-grade benefit case. Merchant needs a counterparty. Hybrid is what most recent US transmission actually does.

steps.name: Federal programme applications (DOE Grid Deployment Office and similar)
steps.note: Capacity-contract and loan mechanisms exist precisely for the phase where a line is not yet fully subscribed.

steps.name: Bond issuance / project finance close
steps._cost_note: Transaction and issuance costs, not the principal raised.
steps.note: The point of no return. Everything cheap and reversible should be resolved before this.
steps._prereq_note: Nested list = any-of. Needs siting authority (state CoN or federal corridor) plus a cost-recovery decision.

steps.name: Financial close reached — construction can begin
steps.note: Carries the project's operating benefit, so the governance and financing chain is ranked by what it actually unlocks rather than treated as costless overhead.

strategies._note: Three coherent routes from the current design to a buildable one. They differ in who carries the risk before construction, not in what gets built.

public_led.label: Public-led / rate base
public_led.note: Traditional regulated build. Slowest gate is the compact plus three certificates of need; no counterparty risk, maximum political exposure.

anchor_led.label: Anchor-tenant led
anchor_led.note: Contract the load first, build to serve it, expand from a revenue base. Trades political risk for counterparty concentration risk.

federal_led.label: Federal corridor led
federal_led.note: Pursue corridor designation and federal financing to reduce state veto risk. Slower to first energization; more robust to any single state stalling.

_prereq_semantics: A prereq entry that is a string is required. A prereq entry that is a list is satisfied by ANY of its members. A step whose prereqs cannot be satisfied within a strategy's include-set is reported as stranded, never silently enabled.
